title: Orders in March
description: Pick out the orders placed between two dates, both ends included.
statement:
Return the `id` and `ordered_at` of every order placed in **March 2025**: from `2025-03-01` to `2025-03-31`, both days included. (Dates are text in the form `YYYY-MM-DD`, which sorts in date order.)

Oldest first, and orders on the same day by `id`.
hints: Which condition keeps values between two limits?
Write the two dates as text in quotes: `'2025-03-01'` and `'2025-03-31'`.
The other data has orders on `2025-02-28`, `2025-03-01`, `2025-03-31` and `2025-04-01`. Which of them belong?
solution:
SELECT id, ordered_at
FROM orders
WHERE ordered_at BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2025-03-31'
ORDER BY ordered_at, id;
explanation:
**The idea.** `BETWEEN a AND b` is `>= a AND <= b`: both ends are included. Dates written as `YYYY-MM-DD` compare correctly as text, because the year comes first, then the month, then the day.

**Watch the ends.** `BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2025-03-31'` works for dates without a time. If the column held timestamps (`2025-03-31 18:30:00`) the last day would be cut off, because `'2025-03-31 18:30:00'` is greater than `'2025-03-31'`. For timestamps the safe form is a half-open range: `>= '2025-03-01' AND < '2025-04-01'`.

**Usual mistakes.** `<` on the last day; an off-by-one on the month end; sorting by `id` only.
